newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin won't get Dietrich street, but metro stop.
newsitem.headline: Berlin won't get Dietrich street, but metro stop.

text.p: Marlene Dietrich may not have a street named after her in Berlin because of lingering opposition to her support of the Allies in World War Two, but a newspaper said on Thursday she may get a metro station instead.

The Bild daily said the Greens party in Berlin has proposed renaming the Papestrasse metro station after the Berlin-born film star, who soared to international fame for her starring role in the 1932 film "The Blue Angel."

Earlier efforts to name a street in the Schoeneberg district of west Berlin where Dietrich was born and raised have been foiled. After a long career in Hollywood, Dietrich died in 1992 in Paris and was buried in Berlin.

Some local Berlin opponents of the street renaming characterised the late actress and singer as a traitor to Germany, but others, including business owners on the street, baulked at the costs and confusion of a new address.
